Okay. His phone is just sitting here and I'm actually doing this. 😬

Okay. Fine. Normal farm thing.

questions.text:
He never mentioned her. Not a niece, not a cousin, nobody. 😔
Twice now he's stepped out of my kitchen to take a call, and both times he said 'Hey, M.'
Who is M?

I've never heard that name. Not once in seven months.
Some weeks he'd surprise me and stay instead of driving north. He'd grin and say 'officially, I'm at a seminar in Ames.'
I thought it was a joke. 🥲
Over the past 60 days, how many 'Ames seminar' nights has he had?

onboarding.text: Jesse left his phone on my nightstand this morning. He won't be back until noon. Seven months together, and there's still a whole part of his life I've never been allowed to see.
onboarding.label: Hallie

onboarding.text: We met at trivia night in the East Village. He's the guy who brings soup when I'm sick and puts gold stars on my spelling tests when I'm too tired to grade. I fell hard. 💛
onboarding.label: Hallie & Jesse

onboarding.text: Jesse Oakes, crop insurance adjuster. Every week he disappears for two days to help his widowed dad on the farm up north. He's never invited me. Not once. He says I'd be bored.
onboarding.label: Jesse

onboarding.text: I don't want to be that girlfriend who snoops. But I need to know what's up there. I'll ask you one thing at a time. Please just tell me the truth, even if it's ugly.
onboarding.label: Hallie

notes.title: Field kit
notes.body:
Truck kit, restock monthly:

- Hail count frame
- Waders / rubber boots
- Clipboard, pencils (pens freeze up, dry out, whatever)
- Sunscreen, bug spray
- Water, at least a gallon
- Tablet charger
- Extra high-vis vest

Low on: pencils, batteries, sunscreen.

10 years married. Don't screw this one up.

notes.title: Corn stage cheat sheet
notes.body:
Quick reminders so I stop googling:
- V-stages count leaves with a visible collar
- VT = tassel, R1 = silk
- Blister, milk, dough, dent, then black layer
- Hail damage this late: look at ear and husk, not just leaf loss
- Green snap after a wind event shows within a day or two

Ask Priya which worksheet the office wants for late-season stand counts.

notes.title: Hail adjust notes
notes.body:
Rule of thumb for corn at V12 to VT: percent leaf loss matters less than stand loss.
Check for bruised stalks, split a few and look for discoloration.
Take photos from the same distance, same angle, with the clipboard in frame.
Every claim: date of loss, field ID, crop stage, estimated yield loss.
RMA tables on the shared drive.
